newsitem.title: YEMEN: Qatar envoy in Yemen with reply on GCC membership.
newsitem.headline: Qatar envoy in Yemen with reply on GCC membership.

text.p: A senior Qatari envoy travelled to Sanaa on Monday to deliver a response from the Gulf Cooperation Council to Yemen's application for membership in the six-nation alliance, official media said.

Yemen's SABA news agency said Qatar's Minister of State for Cabinet Affairs Mohammad bin Khalid al-Thani had arrived in Sanaa and would deliver a letter from Qatar's Emir Sheikh Hamad bin Khalifa al-Thani to Yemeni President Ali Abdullah Saleh.
Qatar's news agency QNA said the letter contained the GCC response to Yemen's application. Qatar currently chairs the political and economic alliance.
The agency did not disclose details of the message and officials were not immediately available for comment.
Yemen formally asked to join the elite club of wealthy Gulf Arab nations at their annual summit in Doha in December.
Gulf analysts believe Yemen's bid would not go beyond granting the impoverished Arab country a favourable status or an observer position in the GCC, which was formed in 1981.
The GCC groups all the other countries of the Arabian peninsula between the Gulf and the Red Sea - Saudi Arabia, Kuwait, Bahrain, Oman, Qatar and the United Arab Emirates (UAE).
Yemen said in its membership request that it qualified to join the group because of its geographic location and its historical ties with the GCC.
Gulf-based diplomats said the UAE, Oman and Qatar favoured Yemen's admission but stopped short of pushing the issue further as arguments about risks and the council's homogeneous structure surfaced.
Yemen is the only country in the peninsula with political parties, opposition newspapers and active Islamist participation in the government.
